items.text: Every device in scope is protected by a correctly configured firewall, or by a network device with firewall functionality.
Default administrative passwords on firewalls are changed to a strong and unique password, or remote administrative access is disabled entirely.

Access to the firewall administrative interface from the internet is prevented, unless there is a clear and documented business need and the interface is protected by multi-factor authentication or by an IP allow list combined with a properly managed password.
Unauthenticated inbound connections are blocked by default.
Inbound firewall rules are approved and documented by an authorised person, including the business need in the documentation.
Unnecessary firewall rules are removed or disabled when they are no longer needed.
A software firewall is used on devices which are used on untrusted networks, such as public wifi hotspots.
Unnecessary user accounts, such as guest accounts and administrative accounts that will not be used, are removed and disabled.
Default or guessable account passwords are changed.
Unnecessary software, including applications, system utilities and network services, is removed or disabled.
Any auto-run feature which allows file execution without user authorisation is disabled.
Users are authenticated before being allowed access to organisational data or services.
Appropriate device locking controls are in place for users that are physically present.
A credential, such as a biometric, password or PIN, is in place before a user can gain access to a device's services.

Device unlocking credentials are protected against brute-force attacks by throttling to no more than 10 guesses in 5 minutes or by locking devices after no more than 10 unsuccessful attempts, or the vendor's default setting is used where neither can be configured.

Device unlocking credentials have a minimum password or PIN length of at least 6 characters where the credential only unlocks the device, and the full password requirements apply where the unlocking credential is also used for authentication.
All software in scope is licensed and supported.
Software is removed from devices when it becomes unsupported, or removed from scope by using a defined sub-set that prevents all traffic to or from the internet.
Automatic updates are enabled where possible.

Software is updated, including vulnerability fixes, within 14 days of release where the vendor describes the vulnerabilities as critical or high risk, where they carry a CVSS v3 base score of 7 or above, or where the vendor provides no details of the level of vulnerabilities the update fixes.
A process is in place to create and approve user accounts.
Users are authenticated with unique credentials before being granted access to applications or devices.
User accounts are removed or disabled when they are no longer required.
Multi-factor authentication is implemented where available, and authentication to cloud services always uses multi-factor authentication.
Separate accounts are used to perform administrative activities only.
Special access privileges are removed or disabled when they are no longer required.
Multi-factor authentication is used for administrative accounts and for accounts accessible from the internet.
The password element of multi-factor authentication has a minimum length of at least 8 characters, with no maximum length restrictions.

Passwords are protected against brute-force password guessing by at least one of multi-factor authentication, throttling to no more than 10 guesses in 5 minutes, or locking devices after no more than 10 unsuccessful attempts.

Password quality is managed by at least one of multi-factor authentication, a minimum password length of at least 12 characters with no maximum length restrictions, or a minimum password length of at least 8 characters with no maximum length restrictions and automatic blocking of common passwords using a deny list.

Users are supported to choose unique passwords for their work accounts by educating them about avoiding common passwords, encouraging the use of three random words, providing usable secure storage for passwords, not enforcing regular password expiry, and not enforcing password complexity requirements.
An established process is in place to change passwords promptly if a password or account is known or suspected to be compromised.
A malware protection mechanism is active on all devices in scope, kept up to date in accordance with the vendor's instructions.
Anti-malware software is updated in line with vendor recommendations.
Anti-malware software prevents malware from running.
Anti-malware software prevents the execution of malicious code.
Anti-malware software prevents connections to malicious websites over the internet.
Only approved applications, restricted by code signing, are allowed to execute on devices, and applications are actively approved before being deployed to devices.
A current list of approved applications is maintained, and users are not able to install any application that is unsigned or has an invalid signature.
